newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians stone Israeli troops in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians stone Israeli troops in Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian youths stoned Israeli troops in the divided West Bank town of Hebron on Tuesday in a fourth straight day of clashes, witnesses said.
The soldiers immediately deployed opposite the youths but withheld fire.
On Monday, soldiers shot and wounded at least 38 Palestinians in clashes at the town.

The violence underscored rising Israel-PLO tensions over a three-month deadlock in peace efforts and what Palestinians view as an Israeli drive to expand Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and Jerusalem and the rest of the West Bank.

Witnesses on Tuesday said several dozen Palestinian boys aged from about 10 to 15 years of age began throwing stones in the area of the Beit Hadassah Jewish enclave. The soldiers have so far refrained from opening fire, they said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority on Monday of ordering violence in Gaza and of doing nothing to stop unrest in Hebron.

"There was a clear set of instructions a few days ago in Gaza for the violence that took place there," Netanyahu told reporters after he addressed a parliamentary committee in Jerusalem, referring to unrest last Thursday.
"I can't tell you about Hebron in the last 24 hours because I haven't seen the reports. But I can tell you that the Palestinian police have refrained from acting against the violence," he said.

Israel handed 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian rule under an interim peace deal in January but kept troops at the heart of the town to protect some 400 Jewish settlers who live there in fortified enclaves.
